'''Deanna Haunsperger''' (born 1964) is an American mathematician. She was the president of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for the 2017–2018 term.<ref name=":0" /> She is a professor of mathematics at [[Carleton College]].<ref name="Faculty Profile Page" />

== Education ==
Haunsperger received her [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in mathematics and [[computer science]] from [[Simpson College]] in 1986. She then received her master's degree in mathematics in 1989 and her Ph.D. in mathematics in 1991 from [[Northwestern University]].<ref name="cv">{{cite web |url=https://apps.carleton.edu/profiles/assets/dhaunspe_cv.pdf |title=Deanna B. Haunsperger Curriculum Vitae |access-date=14 January 2018}}</ref>
Her dissertation was entitled ''Projection and Aggregation Paradoxes in Nonparametrical Statistical Tests'' and her advisor was [[Donald Gene Saari]].<ref name="PHD">{{cite web|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=13611|title=Deanna Haunsperger|website=[[Mathematical Genealogy Project]] |access-date=14 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="PHD on MathSciNet">{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=2686238|title=Projection and aggregation paradoxes in nonparametric statistical tests|website=[[MathSciNet]]|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|last1=Haunsperger|first1=Deanna|access-date=8 April 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==
Haunsperger was an assistant professor of mathematics at [[St. Olaf College]] from 1991 to 1994.<ref name="cv" />
Since 1994, she has been a faculty member in the mathematics department at [[Carleton College]].<ref name="Faculty Profile Page">{{cite web|url=https://apps.carleton.edu/profiles/dhaunspe/|title=Deanna Haunsperger|website=[[Carleton College]] |access-date=14 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="cv" />

From 1995 to 2014, Haunsperger and mathematician Stephen Kennedy directed the Carleton College Summer Mathematics Program for Women. This program worked to prepare undergraduate women to pursue a Ph.D. in mathematics.<ref name="smp">{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.carleton.edu/smp/|title=Summer Mathematics Program for Women Undergraduates |website=Carleton College Department of Mathematics |access-date=14 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="smp ams">{{cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/programs/diversity/Programdescription_2014_Carleton.pdf |title=Carleton College Summer Math Program (SMP) |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |access-date=14 January 2018 |archive-date=15 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915115103/http://www.ams.org/programs/diversity/Programdescription_2014_Carleton.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
From 1999 to 2003, Haunsperger and Kennedy were co-editors of ''[[Math Horizons]]'', a magazine aimed at undergraduate students who are interested in mathematics.<ref name=":0" />

Haunsperger was the second vice-president of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA) from 2006 to 2008. She was elected president of the MAA for the 2017–2018 term.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.maa.org/about-maa/governance/Deanna-Haunsperger|title=Deanna Haunsperger |website=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|access-date=14 January 2018}}</ref>

Haunsperger has won several awards from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM). In 2012, she was selected for the [[M. Gweneth Humphreys Award]], which recognizes mathematics educators who have exhibited outstanding mentorship.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/humphreys-award/ |title=Gweneth Humphreys Awards |website=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]] |access-date=4 May 2020 }}</ref>
She was presented with the second annual AWM Presidential Award in 2017.<ref name=awmpres>{{cite book |last1=Deines |first1=Alyson |last2=Ferrero |first2=Daniela|author2-link=Daniela Ferrero |last3=Graham |first3=Erica |last4=Im |first4=Mee Seong |last5=Manore |first5=Carrie |last6=Price |first6=Candice |date=2018 |title=Advances in the Mathematics Sciences |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=d9p1DwAAQBAJ |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media]] |page=viii |isbn=978-3-319-98683-8 }}</ref>
In 2017, she was selected as a fellow of the AWM in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web| title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows/ |website=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]] |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> She is the 2021 winner of the Yueh-Gin Gung and Dr. Charles Y. Hu Award for Distinguished Service to Mathematics of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] "for her prolific service to mathematics, including with the Mathematical Association of America; for her influential leadership of women in mathematics; for her long focus on inclusion and on building inclusive mathematical communities; and for a laudable career that has been rich in mathematical research, mathematical education, and mathematical exposition".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blogs.ams.org/beyondreviews/2021/01/03/jmm-prizes-and-awards-2021/|title=JMM Prizes and Awards 2021|first=Edward|last=Dunne|publisher=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>
